bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Clear Path for Greener Patna Townships Breaking News Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Clear Path for Greener Patna Townships By Ayesha Siddiqui November 12, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Bihar Building Bylaws 2026, approved by the state cabinet on Tuesday, have received support from real estate entrepreneurs and investors, who said provisions for green construction, rooftop solar, water conservation and a higher floor area ratio could accelerate planned development around Patna. Rajiv Kumar Singh Mantu, group head of a real estate firm, described the approval as a “historic” decision in a communique issued on Wednesday. He said the new rules marked the beginning of a new phase of planned urbanisation, modern satellite townships and eco-friendly green cities across Bihar. The provisions highlighted in the report include green building norms, rooftop solar installations, water conservation measures and an increased floor area ratio, or FAR. FAR determines the amount of floor space that can be built on a plot relative to its area. A higher FAR can allow greater development intensity, although the source report does not specify the revised limits or the conditions attached to them. Mantu said the provisions would support the development of planned satellite townships and modern green cities in and around Patna. The response from the real estate sector links the new bylaws to the state’s wider development plans for areas outside the existing urban core, where new housing, commercial activity and supporting infrastructure are expected to be coordinated through township-scale projects. He specifically referred to the Sonepur development road map and the Gangajal City project, describing them as initiatives aimed at the holistic development of the area. The report does not provide the projects’ investment values, construction schedules, land details or approval status beyond the reference made in the communique. Mantu also expressed hope that the Sonepur City Development Plan would gain momentum following the approval of the bylaws. According to his statement, the plan includes an industrial hub corridor, a greenfield airport and a logistics hub, with the stated objective of developing the area in line with “world standards”. The cabinet approval places the building rules at the centre of Bihar’s proposed urban expansion, but the immediate operational details remain unclear in the available information. The source report does not specify when the bylaws will come into force, which authority will oversee their implementation, how green building and rooftop solar requirements will be assessed, or whether separate notifications and technical guidelines are pending. The approval also comes as developers look to expand beyond established urban areas. In such projects, building regulations determine not only permissible construction but also how environmental measures, land utilisation and new township infrastructure are incorporated into development proposals. The provisions cited by the real estate representative indicate that the state intends to combine higher development potential with measures related to energy and water conservation. Mantu thanked Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, urban development and housing minister Nitish Mishra and MP Rajiv Pratap

national_raw_news.content: Union Cabinet has approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in the North and South Block complex in New Delhi. Briefing the media after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation. The Cabinet has also approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for RABI Season, 2026-27 on Phosphatic and Potassic fertilisers. The tentative budgetary requirement for Rabi 2026-27 will be approximately 62 thousand 370 crore rupees. This is nearly 24 thousand 417 crore more than the budgetary requirement for Rabi 2025-26 season. Mr Vaishnaw said the subsidy will ensure smooth availability of these fertilisers to the farmers at affordable prices. Mr. Vaishnaw said, the Cabinet has approved the continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. He said that the outlay of five thousand crore rupees is approved for guarantee and it is expected to support Mudra loans worth 12.60 lakh crore rupees. The Cabinet has also given nod to the continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and aims to provide financial assistance to an additional 2.5 lakh entrepreneurs in a span of five years. The Cabinet has also cleared the extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04 of Noida Metro Rail Project covering approximately 8.5 kilometres and comprising five elevated stations. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stated that the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum will transform New Delhi into a global centre of cultural heritage, with the world’s largest museum display area. In a social media post, the Prime Minister noted that the Cabinet’s decision will give impetus to the transformation of the historic North and South Block buildings into a magnificent celebration of India’s civilisational journey. Mr Modi said the museum will showcase thousands of years of India’s heritage through world-class galleries and immersive experiences. It will cover a wide range of subjects, including ancient knowledge systems, mathematics, astronomy, architecture, art, languages, and spirituality. He highlighted that these buildings, which have long served as centres of governance, will now become places where millions can discover, experience, and celebrate the timeless richness of India’s civilisation. The Prime Minister described the initiative as a historic new chapter in India’s cultural heritage.

national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu awards nation’s cleanest cities; Visakhapatnam, Indore, Ahmedabad among top winners Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर President Droupadi Murmu awards nation’s cleanest cities; Visakhapatnam, Indore, Ahmedabad among top winners ANI | Updated: Nov 11, 2026 21:58 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 11 (ANI): President Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan 2025–26 awards on Wednesday, honouring India's cleanest urban local bodies and municipal corporations for excellence in waste management and sanitation. In the newly introduced 'Swachh Shehar Jodi' category, which pairs mentor and mentee cities to accelerate urban cleanliness, Ahmedabad and Sanand secured the top rank, followed by Indore and Deopalpur in second, and Tirupati and Kuppam in third. Navi Mumbai, Surat, and Vijayawada emerged as the top three clean cities under the Super Swachh League. Meanwhile, in the million-plus population category, Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC), Jabalpur, and Lucknow were named India's leading sanitation performers. The 2025–26 edition introduced specialised honours for riverfront, coastal, and Himalayan urban centres. According to official data, over 350 urban local bodies (ULBs) jumped more than 500 ranks from the previous cycle, with smaller municipalities playing a leading role as over 1,700 cities with populations under 50,000 improved their standings compared to 2024–25. State-level winners will be recognised during dedicated award ceremonies hosted by their respective state administrations. This year, awards were given for the first time to Swachh River Front Town, Swachh Coastal Town and Clean Himalayan City. According to a press release, President Droupadi Murmu honoured India’s cleanest cities at the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025–26 held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, convened by the Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Winners were felicitated in the presence of Manohar Lal, Union Minister for MoHUA & Power and Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for MoHUA. A total of 60 national awards have been announced this year across seven distinct categories, recognising excellence in urban sanitation and waste management. The honours span the newly introduced Swachh Shehar Jodi (SSJ) category, the Clean Cities of Super Swachh League, and Swachh Shehar across five population brackets. Additional accolades celebrate top performers among Swachh River Front Towns, Swachh Coastal Towns, Clean Himalayan Cities, and State First Swachh Cities, the release stated. Speaking at the event, Droupadi Murmu underscored that cleanliness cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single institution alone and requires active participation from all stakeholders. She emphasised the importance of citizen participation, behavioural change, administrative accountability, and sustained public engagement. Highlighting the need to inculcate cleanliness values from an early age, she called for integrating issues such as plastic waste management into school curricula and fostering continuous dialogue with children and youth. The President noted that meaningful progress in sanitation is possible when citizens, local administrations, and sanitation workers work together, and when the on-ground suggestions of sanitation workers and citizen feedback are given due importance.
